applies_why: The judge text evaluates a collision between the challenger's own seed/loins chain and the defender's chain by describing each chain's footing.
quote: the challenger's seed/loins chain is footed but does not name Joseph as the begetter; the defender's chain is footed but rests on the woman-route inference.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: the phrase 'weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse': reading one, the judge evaluates the two chains by their footing and notes each chain's support; reading two, the judge's 'does not name Joseph' imposes a verse-level naming requirement.
why: The judge compares the two chains by footing and does not rest its result on the retired no-verse-states-contrary test.
